question: Can the exact H100-falsified dual-depth representation be integrated coherently into the pinned v0.5.15 endpoint lifecycle, including dynamic batch transitions and fail-closed graph fallback, without changing the frozen depth rule?
why_now: The exact native H100 consumer passed producer, Triton verification, greedy acceptance, KV movement, scheduler settlement, and graph/eager boundary correctness. The campaign still needs whole-request verify-frequency and economic evidence, while its checkpoint-resident H100 is exclusively claimed by the higher-priority packed-mask endpoint. Offline integration preparation avoids another cold setup and can make adaptive depth immediately runnable on that resident endpoint environment after the current arm finishes.

evidence_interpretation.measured_correctness: The exact H100 component passed all bound producer-to-consumer correctness checks at batch 7/depth 12 and batch 8/depth 6.
evidence_interpretation.directional_timing_only: The larger batch-8/depth-6 eager arm had a 0.397040 ms median combined interval versus 0.414096 ms for batch-7/depth-12 CUDA graph, a 4.12% directional advantage despite the larger batch.
evidence_interpretation.measurement_shortfall: The result contains 100 repetitions per arm, whereas the director component binding requested at least 200 per valid arm. Treat timing as underpowered and non-comparative because batch size, depth, and execution mode all differ.
evidence_interpretation.forbidden_inference: The component does not establish an isolated same-batch depth delta, whole-request latency, acceptance, sustainable throughput, quality, or economics.

research_contract.implementation: Mechanically verify every bound hash. In one project-local pinned v0.5.15 source tree, integrate exactly the frozen rule: depth 12 for batches 1 through 7 and depth 6 for batches 8 and above. Preserve the dual native producers, active-depth metadata, ragged prior-result ownership, active scheduler stride, depth-12 graph admission, and strict depth-6 eager fallback proven by the bound artifacts.
research_contract.endpoint_lifecycle: Trace and implement endpoint-facing configuration and state transitions from scheduler admission through speculative worker invocation, target verification, acceptance, KV settlement, request completion, and the next scheduling cycle. Do not alter the model, workload, threshold, depths, acceptance algorithm, or endpoint request contract.
research_contract.quality_gate: Pass positive and fail-closed CPU/state fixtures for batches 1, 7, 8, and above; transitions 7-to-8-to-7; request permutation; cancellation and completion; partial and empty NGRAM matches; reused request slots; graph replay admission; eager fallback; result ownership; and scheduler/KV offsets. Any stale depth, padded depth disguise, cross-request ownership, or producer-consumer disagreement closes the candidate.
research_contract.handoff: Produce an immutable endpoint-integration source manifest and exact launch/config delta suitable for one later whole-request stock/candidate comparison. The later endpoint remains separately director-authorized and must use fresh requests; this preparation does not authorize a provider claim or endpoint sample.
research_contract.terminal: Persist ADAPTIVE_DEPTH_ENDPOINT_INTEGRATION_RESULT.json and ADAPTIVE_DEPTH_ENDPOINT_INTEGRATION_DECISION.md by 2026-07-25T15:30:00Z. Classify the result endpoint_ready_offline, transferred_negative, or integration_infeasible.

budgets.storage: At most 2 GiB of project-local source, fixtures, manifests, and reports.

prohibitions: Do not claim, inspect, poll, signal, or mutate any provider GPU.
Do not inspect or modify the packed-mask project or its claimed endpoint bench.
Do not stage or load a checkpoint.
Do not submit an endpoint request, historical request, or sentinel.
Do not repeat the H100 component timing or infer endpoint economics from it.
Do not sweep threshold, depth, graph policy, or representation variants.
Do not create a successor or repair project; retain this project and scientific lineage.
